overview: This appears to be the tail end of a Marathon County Human Resources, Finance, and Property Committee meeting. The brief transcript captures only the final minutes, including a summary of prior consensus decisions regarding Rib Mountain law enforcement contract negotiations and a Wisconsin Public Service easement at the Sunnyville property, along with adjournment. No substantive votes on new matters were recorded in the available transcript.

discussions.item: Rib Mountain Law Enforcement Contract and Sunnyville Easement Negotiations
discussions.body: The presiding official summarized a prior consensus directing administration to continue negotiations with the Village of Rib Mountain on a law enforcement services contract and to negotiate with Wisconsin Public Service on easement costs at the Sunnyville property. It was noted that any resulting agreement must return to this committee and ultimately to the full board for approval. No new debate occurred on these items in the available transcript.

discussions.item: Sales Tax Update and Year-to-Date Budget Updates
discussions.body: The presiding official noted that the sales tax update and year-to-date budget updates were included in the meeting packets and available for members to read independently, and moved past these items without discussion.

An official — identified only as Vice Chair — flagged that the committee had inadvertently skipped the fee policy discussion. The presiding official acknowledged this and indicated it would be addressed, though no substantive discussion took place in the available transcript.

discussions.item: Next Meeting — Joint Meeting with Portage County at Central Wisconsin Airport
discussions.body: The committee was informed that the next meeting is scheduled for September 14 at 5:00 p.m. at the Central Wisconsin Airport. This is described as an annual joint meeting with Portage County to discuss the airport budget, as required by the bylaws governing the Central Wisconsin Airport.
A motion to adjourn was made and seconded by Supervisor Hart. The motion carried on a voice vote with no audible opposition.
